title: Interface Control Record
body:
Overview

This is Manon's original Signature counterpart for Interface Control Record inside the Mission Systems Integration Signature Database, built as part of the Signature ecosystem rather than copied from any outside source. Maps interfaces, dependencies, system requirements and integration tests. The Signature edition keeps the same discipline as the public edition: every entry states the task, shows the method in full, and carries a demo program that was genuinely executed at build time, so the result shown is a result that actually ran. Signature records are labeled as Signature originals wherever they appear, and they never present a design as an established fact. A design is called a design, a measured result is called a measured result, and the difference is kept visible in the record itself.

How it works

The method in each record is interface-first engineering: every connection between parts of a system is written down as a contract naming the data, the format, the timing, and the error behavior. Integration tests then check each contract directly, and a requirement is only marked satisfied when its test passes. This is support engineering for complex platforms: making parts work together reliably.

Worked detail

The worked detail for this Signature entry is concrete and reproducible. The accompanying demo program ran at build time and its output begins with: contracts checked: 5. The complete program and its full output travel with this record, so any reader can re-run the code and confirm the result independently. The Signature version adapts the public method to Signature conventions: the same checks, the same honesty about limits, and the same requirement that a claim travel no further than its evidence. Where this entry describes a procedure, the steps are ordered and checkable; where it describes a model, the inputs, the calculation, and the uncertainty are all stated; where it describes a plan, the constraints are named first, because a plan that hides its constraints cannot be trusted when conditions change.

Use and ladder

An integration team uses these records to plan test order, to trace a failure to the contract it broke, and to prove that a change in one part did not silently break another. Teaching ladder: this record is ranked simple. Simple Signature records introduce one idea at a time, compounded records combine ideas into a working procedure, and most-complex records carry the full procedure with its edge cases and limits. Feasibility tier: established. Implementation status: established. When the status is designed, this record offers a design plus an executed demo; deployment is not claimed. The Signature edition stands alongside the public edition as Manon's own original counterpart, and both editions are linked from the database page so readers can compare them.

# Interface Control Record: check every interface contract and report completeness.
contracts = [('data format', True), ('timing', True), ('error behavior', True), ('versioning', False), ('security boundary', True)]
passed = [name for name, ok in contracts if ok]
failed = [name for name, ok in contracts if not ok]
print("contracts checked:", len(contracts))
print("passed:", len(passed), passed)
print("failed:", len(failed), failed)
print("integration ready:", not failed)

passed: 4 ['data format', 'timing', 'error behavior', 'security boundary']
failed: 1 ['versioning']
integration ready: False
